source_code_version: IsaacLab v2.3.2 tag, not asserted byte-identical to the recovered training runtime

sources.title: IsaacLab v2.3.2 common MDP reward functions
sources.quote: Reward tracking of linear velocity commands (xy axes) using exponential kernel.
verified_facts: XY reward is exp(-sum((command_xy-root_lin_vel_b_xy)^2)/std^2); yaw reward is exp(-(command_yaw-root_ang_vel_b_z)^2/std^2).
Torque cost uses summed squared applied torque; action-rate cost uses summed squared differences between consecutive actions.
Flat orientation uses squared XY projected gravity. It is not a body-height or joint-posture target.
is_terminated_term masks timeouts, and is_terminated reads true terminations rather than timeouts.
sources.transfer_limit: Saved cfg identifies symbol/std but does not establish the exact installed function body. Extra reward terms or std changes exceed a weights-only interface unless rules explicitly allow them.

sources.title: IsaacLab v2.3.2 velocity locomotion reward functions
verified_facts: It is gated by commanded XY speed norm greater than 0.1, not by yaw command.
With threshold 0.5, landings after shorter air intervals contribute negative values before weighting.
This term does not explicitly measure foot clearance, foot placement, slip, or gait phase.
sources.transfer_limit: This is the upstream quadruped method. Exact installed body must be checked before diagnosing training. Threshold/gating/function replacement is not a weight-only change.

sources.title: Learning Agile and Dynamic Motor Skills for Legged Robots
sources.quote: All of cost terms are multiplied by this curriculum factor
verified_facts: Objective costs are exempt while other costs increase through a multiplicative factor.
The paper uses k0=0.3 and k_(j+1)=k_j^0.997, converging toward 1.
The experiment uses ANYmal, learned actuator dynamics and TRPO, with distinct state/history/reset and termination settings.
sources.transfer_limit: Evidence for a particular curriculum method, not evidence that B1 checkpoint500 switched to F10 will improve Go2. Its coefficients, time scale, training state and model differ.

sources.title: Learning to Walk in Minutes Using Massively Parallel Deep Reinforcement Learning
sources.quote: The solution is to distinguish the two termination modes
verified_facts: Terrain difficulty follows per-environment progress and can decrease on insufficient progress.
Success at the highest terrain level is followed by random level assignment, so a mean terrain level is not a globally monotonic score.
The paper distinguishes timeout bootstrapping from failure termination.
It trains a single policy with the same rewards across terrain types.
sources.transfer_limit: Supports terrain/reset semantics and comparing fixed scenarios, not score forecasts or an arbitrary B1-to-F10 reward switch. Its timing/performance cannot be transferred to the competition runtime.

sources.title: Walk These Ways: Tuning Robot Control for Generalization with Multiplicity of Behavior
sources.quote: we force the total reward to be a positive linear function of the task reward
verified_facts: Total reward is task_reward * exp(0.02 * negative_auxiliary_reward), rather than a plain additive sum.
The method adds behavior commands, contact/gait reward structure, and a grid command curriculum.
Table 4 reports a gait-free flat-ground tracking baseline with XY/yaw rewards 0.94/0.76 versus trotting 0.92/0.70.
The paper also reports task-dependent benefits from behavior control; flat-ground tracking is not the only target.
sources.transfer_limit: Gait constraints do not universally improve tracking. These results are from another robot/training setup and do not prove that removing Go2 feet_air_time improves rough-terrain scoring.

allowed_scope_assumption: Only the existing ten scalar reward weights may change; root task independently audits current rules. All proposed relaxations remain unimplemented.

hypotheses.name: Fixed-sum tracking-axis allocation
hypotheses.allowed_now: Conditional on root confirming the ten-weight bounds
hypotheses.rationale: Keep the maximum positive tracking-coefficient sum at 3.5 and vary XY:yaw preference independently of total tracking escalation.
hypotheses.evidence_level: Mechanism certain if upstream code matches; improvement evidence weak; diagnostic value moderate.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: No fixed-scenario VX improvement or yaw/survival regression. Existing F10 benefit from raising yaw is counterevidence to assume yaw can safely be reduced.
hypotheses.warning: Example coefficients are a falsifiable comparison point, not an optimum. The sum is a maximum reward bound, not equal expected reward or identical PPO updates.

hypotheses.name: Fixed objective with gradual non-task cost curriculum
hypotheses.requires: Explicit permission for a reward schedule and verified training/resume-state semantics
hypotheses.evidence_level: Strong precedent for the mechanism on ANYmal; unvalidated Go2 transfer.
hypotheses.design_constraint: Hold tracking weights/ratio and reward functions fixed, vary only a prespecified cost schedule; do not call a simultaneous B1-to-F10 switch an isolated curriculum.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: Early advantage fails to persist under matched final reward/iteration/evaluation, or survival regresses.
hypotheses.warning: The published k0 and exponent are references, not a proposed optimal Go2 schedule.

hypotheses.name: Match tracking-kernel sensitivity and command difficulty to observed errors
hypotheses.requires: Permission for std/command curriculum/function changes plus actual per-step error distributions
hypotheses.evidence_level: Official kernel mathematics and command-curriculum precedent; no current evidence that B1 is kernel-saturated.
hypotheses.design_constraint: Measure large-error occupancy first. A wider initial kernel or easier commands is only a conditional hypothesis; fine tracking and survival remain heldout targets.
hypotheses.disconfirmation: Large-error occupancy is small, or shaping raises logged reward without reducing fixed-scenario RMSE.
hypotheses.warning: A small derivative with respect to physical error is not proof that PPO has zero policy gradient.
